newsitem.title: UK: Pound lower after British rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Pound lower after British rate rise.

text.p: Sterling fell sharply against the mark but firmed versus the dollar on Thursday afternoon after intially swinging violently on a 25-basis point interest rate rise in Britain.
The Dutch central bank followed later in the day with a 0.10-point increase in its special advances rate to 3.00 percent, which pushed the dollar to session lows.
Most European bourses, more focused on the British rate rise and earlier comments from German central bank members that sent the dollar lower, got only limited support from Wall Street's higher open.
The Dow later slid into negative territory.
London stocks eventually edged up on relief that the Bank of England's (BOE) expected rate rise was only a quarter point to 6.75 percent instead of the half point some analysts had forecast.
But for SocGen strategist Andy Hartwill the quarter point rise came as no surprise.

"This was entirely expected as far as the equity market is concerned," said Hartwill. "Maybe we can sit back for a while and wait for these rises to take effect. The market will like it a damned sight more than 50 basis points."
Others said the smaller rate rise was disheartening because it made the Bank of England (BOE) seem soft on inflation.

"I would have hoped that the Bank of England would roar but in fact, it hasn't," said Richard Jeffrey, chief economist at Charterhouse. "I think we will look back on these rate rises and conclude that (the BOE) was not aggressive enough...I think we'll eventually see the market come off."
Sterling and the dollar were already losing against the mark when the rate rise was announced because of earlier comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.

Sterling briefly recovered to 2.9750 marks from a low of 2.9513 hit just after the rate announcement as investors bought at the lows. But it just as quickly resumed its slide towards session lows, trading at 2.9545 in the late afternoon.
Tietmeyer said Germany's central bank was watching foreign exchange market developments closely and that the dollar's sharp rise against the mark was now over.
"We will naturally watch the developments in markets," he said. "You can be sure that it is important for us that the mark remains a strong currency, and we enter the euro as a strong currency."
The euro is the planned single European currency to be launched on January 1, 1999.
Tietmeyer also said: "I think the British pound very strongly reflects the domestic situation."
The dollar slid further against the mark after the Dutch raised rates to boost the guilder against the mark.
The Dutch rate increase was seen reinforcing ideas that interest rates in Germany may have bottomed. Some traders closely watch the Dutch rate moves as a prelude to German moves.
More Tietmeyer comments, coupled with the dollar's fall, also pressured German shares, forcing the 30-share DAX to snap its seven consecutive record high closes.
Tietmeyer said the DAX's surge did not reflect the health of the entire German economy.

Profit-taking in the DAX index also emerged as investors rushed to take profits after the Bundesbank said it was closely watching the DAX's recent sharp gains. The DAX scored a record high of 4,066.09 on Wednesday.
But traders expected the DAX's losses to be short-lived. "This appears to be a one-day reversal for now. But it may be time for some consolidation," a Frankfurt dealer said.

In Paris, domestic appliance maker SEB SA was the biggest loser, sliding 5.78 percent to 1,060 French francs by 1450 GMT. Dealers noted SEB's continental Europe sales fell despite a 17-percent overall rise in first-half sales.
In metals markets, London gold was fixed at $319.80 per ounce in the afternoon compared with Wednesday's close of $319.75.

Dealers expected gold prices to drift up, recovering some of its losses to 12-year lows. "I think we have seen the lows, and the next move is toward $325" this week, a dealer at a major Swiss bank said.
But traders said sentiment remained bearish and heavy selling could reemerge next week.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 113.07 yen and 1.7510 marks compared with 112.97 and 1.7612 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.8 points at 4,765.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trading down 63.48 points at 3,992.38.
PARIS - The CAC-40 dropped 21.24 points to 2,929.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $319.80 per ounce in the afternoon, compared with Wednesday's close of $319.75. Silver was set at $4.33 versus Wednesday's close at $4.34.
